questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to go on exchange because of the academic opportunities but also very much because of the social experience. I was supposed to go to Vancouver in Canada, but due to Covid-19 I ended up applying within EU, too. I chose Stockholm as I have only heard good things about the university and the city. I also wanted to go to a place with a high academic level. Here, Karolinska ranks as the 6th best medical university in the world, and I therefore think that going there was an exciting opportunity in light of my career and to receive some of the best teaching worldwide within my field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only minus, and why I don't give a 10-mark, is because Stockholm is not that great a city for students. Karolinska moreover wasn't that a social university with a big student community, bars, and parties (maybe also in light of Covid-19). As I really was seeking the social experience on my exchange this became a small minus. Furthermore, Swedes are (like Danes) quite isolated, and it's hard to mingle with them. The educational program, I followed, was international (6 out of 60 persons were Swedish), so it was not a problem in school. The international/exchange student community was amazing, the academic level was outstanding, the housing was great, and Stockholm is beautiful and very cool, so everything else would get a 10-mark.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The Karolinska Institute was extremely easy to be an exchange student on - both before you arrive and when you're there. Their website is super informative and intuitive, it's easy to understand their platform and find which courses they offer. Furthermore, the exchange coordinator Giulia is absolutely the sweetest and most helpfull person ever, and you can always reach out to her before, during, and after your exchange.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. A girl from my educational program in Denmark, also went so we figured everything out together. Not that it is hard: you get your schedule and try to find the courses the first days, and then it becomes more and more easy. They didn't have a buddy program in autumn 2021, which could have been nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The Karolinska Institute offers housing through KI housing. KI housing have accommodations multiple places all over the city. Many of the students housing opportunities are run-down and "trashed" as you'll find student accommodations almost everywhere. I chose to apply for the entirely new Solna Residence which is located on-campus. They finished it 1 week before I arrived, so everything was like an IKEA warehouse and super-new and nice. I had a studio with shared kitchen where we were 20 people sharing a very large kitchen on each floor. Our rooms of around 22m2 consisted of an entrance with mini-kitchen, a large bathroom, a walk-in, and a bed/livingroom. It was amazing. Furthermore, we had a large shared community room in each building for get-togethers. The laundry options was AMAZING. Everything regarding housing would get a 10+. :-)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchen was super nice and well equipped with 3 stoves, 3 ovens, 10 microwaves, 2 large fridges (we also had fridge and freezer in our own rooms), rice cooker etc. etc. We shared it 20 people. There's not possibility for meal plans, but we always ate around 6-10 people together. Super cozy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Choose Solna residence. I will recommend studio with shared kitchen and not your own studio (very expensive) or shared kitchen with 2/4 people. Shared with 20 people gives great possibilities to get to know a lot of people, and there are always people to talk to. Super nice when you're away from friends and family. Moreover, you have your own bathroom and apartment, so you can just go to your room if you need a bit space (compared to shared with 2/4 people).

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a long time since I applied, but KI and KU really makes it easy and convenient for you. Erasmus is quite straight forward - just note the deadlines and you'll be fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: KI and KU can always help you and are super sweet with a lot of support.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. I had "Oncology" and "Cardiometabolics and Infectious diseases". Both courses was 15 ECTS.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's quite easy - don't stress about it. I was very happy with my courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is a little lower than at KU. You have MUCH more free time on exchange compared to at home. Furthermore, it's only failed, pass or pass with destination, which make all academics more chill. The exams are so nice, as they give you a lot of time so you don't have to stress and so you have the possibility to sit and think about your answers.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had lectures, a few lab exercises, problem based learning (like SAU at SUND on Uni of Copenhagen, but where you are 6-8 students and TWO professors working together for 8 weeks - its really really cool and one of the best experiences academically), a few journal clubs, and only a few written assignments in "Cardiometabolics and infectious diseases".

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BACH-Molecular medicine - oncology (15 ECTS) in English , End August - Beginning November

BACH-Molecular medicine - cardiometabolic and infectious diseases (15 ECTS) in English
, Beginning November - Mid January

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both - I really, really loved "Oncology". It was amazing. We met patients, designed trials, had great lectures, and it was super well structured. "Cardiometabolics and infectious diseases" was super nice, and a very good deep introduction to some of the biggest killers worldwide. Both courses both revolved around molecular aspects but also more clinical than the courses I have had on SCIENCE and SUND in Copenhagen. I would really recommend you to take both courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None - everything is quite like in DK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is a bit more expensive in the supermarked. We ended up eating out a lot to get the full experience - remember Fika at least 4 times a week. Alcohol is SOOOO expensive (215 SEK for the cheapest bottle of alcohol). Traveling back and forth to CPH is super cheap by train if you plan 2 months ahead (like 150 DKK pr way). SAS has very convenient youth tickets too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We had a gym and sports courts which were super nice, and saved you for a gym membership. Student clubs were missing which was so sad.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much - our exchange coordinator (Giulia) was amazing to plan activities and dinners, but besides that the social part of Karolinska wasn't that impressive. The first day us 5 exchange people in my class found each other, and we had a blast for 5 months. They a friends for life <3

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Tyresta national park. Go out eating a lot and live in a luxury bubble. Allow your self to spend extra money. Go to as many Christmas markets as possible. Go to Skansen Christmas market. Eat at 800 degrees, Greasy spoon, and Dino sushi. Watch a ballet in the opera. Go to the fotografiska museum and Vasa museum. Go to the cinema. Have the time of you life.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and see the beautiful nature. Take long walks. Find new places for Fika.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local culture is quite like Denmark - except Fika, which is something we need to import to DK. It's very nice and easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I drank a lot of coffees and invited people out that I met to socialize. Be outgoing and just ask if you meet a nice person if they want to hang out, go the the museum, or a coffee. That's the vibe and way to meet new friends. Furthermore, I also took lead on planning dinners in our common kitchen and signed up for hikes at the university. Go for it - you have nothing to loose.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Swedes a very isolated, and actually don't truly like the Danish at first. You need to loosen them up, and then you'll found out that they are quite like us :))) KI don't offer language courses to Danish and Norwegian exchange students even though danish people don't understand people from Stockholm and vice versa.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika :-P And the lot of free time and Christmas vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be social and outgoing.
Spend extra money on yourself. 
Eat lots of Fika (I recommend Lillebrors bageri, Stora bageriet, Kaffeverket and Pascal).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that's its hard to leave your best friends and family. You have used your whole life finding your friends in DK, so it takes time and energy to find new good friends in a new city. Use that time and energy. Make a nice vibe in your shared kitchen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social experience with us 5 exchange student (2 danish and 3 dutch) and the academic experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find out what really matters to you, when you have time to rethink you're everyday life in a new setting.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
